resolvedOrSuperseded.resolvedBy: §268. Three controls, all enforced server-side BEFORE the pre-spend claim and therefore before the transport is reachable: an explicit Expert kill switch (EXPERT_EXECUTION_ENABLED), a per-workspace analysis ceiling, and a per-workspace cost ceiling. All three are evaluated by one pure function, `evaluateExpertExecutionPermission`, with the kill switch checked FIRST so an emergency disable works even when the usage accounting is the thing that is broken.
resolvedOrSuperseded.killSwitch: Production must set EXPERT_EXECUTION_ENABLED to exactly "true" or "false"; boot fails otherwise, so its production value is a decision rather than a default. Disabling refuses Expert EXECUTION only — the deterministic workflow, reads of existing Expert analyses, and settlement of analyses already awaiting confirmation all keep working. Settlement stays available deliberately: disabling it too would strand every analysis already in ANALYSIS_AWAITING_CONFIRMATION and block inspection completion.
resolvedOrSuperseded.costAccounting: The §266 gap — ExpertLegResponse drops usage, so the cost columns were never populated — is closed WITHOUT touching a frozen file. `ExpertLegResponse` lives in expert-hazlenz-analysis.ts, which is element 5 of the §259 candidate identity, and anthropic-expert-provider.ts is a protected module. So usage travels beside the response through `ExpertLegUsageReporter`, a side channel on the seam: the hosted transport already parses the provider envelope and now keeps `usage.input_tokens`/`output_tokens` instead of discarding them. Recorded for EVERY outcome, in a `finally`, because refusals and truncated answers spend too.
resolvedOrSuperseded.legAccounting: Per LEG, never per analysis. §255 measured an unconditional verifier leg, so one analysis is not one provider call. Measured: an analysis reaching the verifier records 2 legs; one whose verifier is deliberately not reached records 1.
resolvedOrSuperseded.boundedRetry: One attempt per leg — there is no automatic retry anywhere on the product path, so worst-case spend is bounded by the leg count rather than by a retry policy. A human retry reuses the idempotency key and resolves to the execution that already ran.

resolvedOrSuperseded.resolvedBy: docs/operations/ROLLBACK_MODEL.md. The governing rule is that a database rollback must never destroy human settlements or Expert analyses in order to restore older application code. The supported path is APPLICATION ROLLBACK ONTO A FORWARD-MIGRATED SCHEMA: all three backlog migrations are additive and backward-compatible with the previous application version, which is why /health/ready treats a database AHEAD of the running build as READY rather than as a fault.
resolvedOrSuperseded.migrationDownPolicy: Production rollback is NOT "run every DOWN". All three are forward-only once real beta data exists, and TWO OF THE THREE ENFORCE IT THEMSELVES: 1800000020000 already refuses when settlements exist (§264 built that in), and 1800000021000 cannot recreate the stricter single-current index on any observation carrying both a current deterministic and a current Expert analysis — the normal state after any Expert run. 1800000019000 does NOT self-enforce and its DOWN would destroy every execution record and Expert provenance column; it must never be run against a database that has served beta traffic. If the schema genuinely must go backward, restore the pre-deployment backup and accept the documented write loss.
resolvedOrSuperseded.caveatRecorded: Rolling application code back past §267 while 1800000021000 remains applied reintroduces the §266 P0-2 selection defect for the duration, because the relaxed index lets the old query find two current rows. Documented, with the instruction to set EXPERT_EXECUTION_ENABLED=false at the same time.

resolvedOrSuperseded.resolvedBy: §268 regenerated verification/current/MUTATING-SCRIPTS.json with the §263 classifier. It now carries 1049 scripts (was 1005) and classifies test-265-expert-product-acceptance as WRITES_HISTORICAL_OUTPUT / sandbox-required, listing it under writesAcceptedHistoricalEvidence, alongside entries for test-264, test-267 and the two §268 suites.
resolvedOrSuperseded.classifierExtended: Two minimal extensions, each closing a case where the registry was structurally unable to see or correctly label a real mutator. (1) It scanned `.ts` only, so the §268 release scripts — plain JavaScript precisely so they run in the production image without ts-node — were invisible, including the one that migrates production schema. (2) Its database-mutation pattern recognised only the CLI form `migration:run`, so scripts/release/migrate.js was classified READ_ONLY; it now also recognises `runMigrations` and `undoLastMigration` and is correctly MUTATES_DATABASE.
resolvedOrSuperseded.mutationSafetyRule: §268 required that normal verification not run evidence writers in write mode. All three evidence-writing suites (§265, §267, §268) now route their writes through one shared gate, `scripts/lib/evidence-write-gate.ts`, off unless HAZLENZ_WRITE_EVIDENCE=1. No assertion is gated — only the side effect of overwriting an accepted package — which is what lets hazlenz:evidence mean "something changed" rather than "a suite ran again".

resolvedOrSuperseded.statement: Report generation returns 500 in every environment checked, because no object storage is configured.
resolvedOrSuperseded.measured: neither STORAGE_S3_BUCKET nor STORAGE_LOCAL_ROOT is set
resolvedOrSuperseded.consequence: No report, no photo evidence, no PDF. §266 also establishes that this now GATES BOOT rather than only failing at runtime: validate-production-environment requires STORAGE_S3_BUCKET, so production cannot start without it. That is the right behaviour and it makes provisioning a hard precondition of deployment rather than a surprise.
resolvedOrSuperseded.requiredAction: provision the bucket and set STORAGE_S3_* in a section authorized to do so
resolvedOrSuperseded.closureProof: one upload and one download round-trip against the provisioned bucket
resolvedOrSuperseded.resolution: The premise was false for production. The P0 said "no object storage is configured"; that was measured locally. Production has STORAGE_PROVIDER=s3 and a Cloudflare R2 bucket insite-production, and the application cannot boot without STORAGE_S3_BUCKET. §269 verified the live bucket end to end with a synthetic non-customer object: upload, authorised download with sha256 match, unsigned GET and LIST both refused, no public bucket policy, delete, and zero residue. The bucket already holds objects under the evidence/ and report/ prefixes.
resolvedOrSuperseded.residual: The product-route report round-trip is release-sequence step 9. The storage DEPENDENCY that this P0 named is closed.

resolvedOrSuperseded.statement: No error-monitoring or structured-logging dependency exists in either workspace. Observability is console output plus /health, /health/live, /health/ready and /health/version.
resolvedOrSuperseded.measured: no sentry/datadog/otel/pino/winston dependency in backend or frontend package.json
resolvedOrSuperseded.consequence: A beta whose stated purpose is learning from real use would run blind. Nothing would tell the team that analyses are failing, that users are stuck awaiting confirmation, that settlement is erroring, or that authorization failures are spiking. The product already writes rich security_audit_events and expert_analysis_executions rows — the data exists; nothing surfaces it.
resolvedOrSuperseded.requiredAction: minimum: backend error reporting with release tagging, plus one operational query or dashboard over expert_analysis_executions (failures, awaiting-confirmation age) and security_audit_events (entitlement_denied, authorization failures).
resolvedOrSuperseded.closureProof: unchanged: an induced failure appears in a monitoring surface within one minute. Emission alone does not satisfy it.
resolvedOrSuperseded.§268emissionClosed: A closed vocabulary of 17 structured operational events now exists on the `safety-insite.operational-event.v1` schema, covering Expert execution start/admit/refuse/unresolved/fail, provider transport and verifier failure, usage recorded, kill-switch and spend-limit refusals, request-version conflicts, confirmation required and settled, storage and report failures, and schema-readiness and migration failures. Redaction is BY CONSTRUCTION: metadata values are coerced to bounded scalars and any key whose NAME looks credential- or content-bearing is dropped, so passing an observation to the emitter does not log the observation. Proven: no raw provider output, no observation text, no credential, no reviewer prose in any emitted event.
resolvedOrSuperseded.§268stillOpen: INGESTION. §268 forbids calling console output monitoring and this register will not. Nothing collects, retains, alerts on or routes these events; there is still no error-monitoring or structured-logging dependency in either workspace. Every candidate destination ingests structured stdout, so emitting the canonical shape first and choosing a destination second is the order that does not have to be undone — but the destination is unchosen and unprovisioned.
resolvedOrSuperseded.resolution: A real collector exists and was verified ingesting live. §269 induced a production request at a unique path and retrieved that exact record from the Render log store seconds later with structured labels (method, statusCode, host, path, level, type). Render indexes app and request streams by level, type, path, status and time. §268 emission is severity-routed so warning and error land on stderr and are labelled accordingly. An operator review command (npm run ops:events) and a signal-to-responder table (docs/operations/MONITORING_AND_ALERTING.md) turn that from reviewable-in-principle into reviewed-in-practice. Push alerting on service failure is Render notifyOnFail.
resolvedOrSuperseded.residual: The §268 event VOCABULARY has never appeared in production because the emitting code is not deployed. First observation of a real operational event is a release-sequence verification step. §269 verified the shape instead: 8 of 8 representative events emitted by the compiled emitter parsed back by the reviewer, with a planted provider key, observation text and Authorization header all reduced to [redacted].
resolvedOrSuperseded.notClaimed: The emission layer is not reported as monitoring. The collector, not the emitter, is what closes this.

verdict.question: Is the current Safety InSite v1.0 product ready for a controlled human beta?
verdict.answer: NOT YET — and what remains is no longer engineering.
verdict.why: The LIVE INFRASTRUCTURE lane is effectively closed. §269 verified deployment control on both platforms, the running production SHA, the production database and its migration state, a defensible backup with a byte-verified restore rehearsal, production object storage end to end, the full production security configuration, the instance shape, spend ceilings resolved from the live environment, and a real log collector ingesting production events. It also found and fixed the single condition that would have made the release fail: EXPERT_EXECUTION_ENABLED was absent, and the beta candidate could not have booted in production without it. What is left in Lane A are execution steps that belong to the release by design — run the migrations, set the provider credential, deploy the named SHA, run one smoke. What is left in Lane B is not engineering at all: all seven legal artifacts are drafted, and none can be closed by engineering because closing them is a counsel review and an explicit product-owner classification.
verdict.measuredNotInferred: §269 contacted production read-only except for five authorized environment-variable writes and one Vercel project setting. 0 provider analysis calls, 0 production migrations, 0 production database writes, 0 application pushes, 0 application deploys. The running SHA was verified unchanged after every configuration change.
